title: Journey events, error-boundary reports, and performance marks
iWant: stable, named signals from every journey and failure
soThat: we can see where users struggle without instrumenting after the fact

acceptanceCriteria.description: Every checkpoint in the journey inventory emits its declared event with the ADR-209 naming scheme; emitted names match the registry exactly.
acceptanceCriteria.then: every checkpoint event fires with its registered name

acceptanceCriteria.description: Events carry the declared minimal context (route, journey step, outcome) and never include personal data beyond the declared allow-list.
acceptanceCriteria.then: context is present and no disallowed personal data appears

acceptanceCriteria.description: Error boundaries exist at shell and route level; a component crash renders the designed error state per application-spa-REQ-010 instead of a white screen, and reports the catch with route and component context.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a component forced to throw during render
acceptanceCriteria.then: the designed error state renders and one report is emitted

acceptanceCriteria.description: Performance marks fire at first paint and time-to-interactive with the reserved registry names.
acceptanceCriteria.then: both marks fire once each with correct names

acceptanceCriteria.description: With no telemetry backend configured, instrumentation no-ops cleanly: no console errors, no failed requests, no behavioural difference.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a deployment without a telemetry endpoint

acceptanceCriteria.description: Given the offline telemetry buffer's configured bound N and (N + 5) events emitted while offline, when the transport comes back online, then only the newest N events survive the buffer's drop-oldest policy and flush to the transport in emission order; the drop count is observable via a `telemetryBuffered` boot record on reconnect and the pre-overflow events are absent from the delivered stream.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an offline session with (N + 5) telemetry events emitted against a buffer bound of N
acceptanceCriteria.then: the newest N events flush in emission order and the drop count is observable on reconnect
